Fact.Name: New Mexico low-income exemption ceiling, single
Fact.Description: PIT-1 line 14 worksheet. A single filer with federal AGI of $36,667 or less qualifies for the low- and middle-income exemption. That exemption, the low-income comprehensive tax rebate, and the working families tax credit are not calculated, so the return stops at this ceiling. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, page PIT-1-26.

Fact.Name: New Mexico low-income exemption ceiling, married filing jointly
Fact.Description: PIT-1 line 14 worksheet. A joint return with federal AGI of $55,000 or less qualifies for the low- and middle-income exemption. That exemption, the low-income comprehensive tax rebate, and the working families tax credit are not calculated, so the return stops at this ceiling. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, page PIT-1-26.

Fact.Name: New Mexico tax rate table limit
Fact.Description: Line 17 of $100,000 or less uses the tax rate table. Line 17 over $100,000 uses the worksheet on page T-7. 2025 Tax Rate Table, page T-7: If line 17 of Form PIT-1 (Taxable Income) is over $100,000 use the following table.

Fact.Name: New Mexico tax table first row ceiling
Fact.Description: The first tax-table row is more than $0 but not over $60. Its Single and joint tax is $0. 2025 Tax Rate Table, page T-1.

Fact.Name: New Mexico tax table second row ceiling
Fact.Description: The second tax-table row is more than $60 but not over $100. Its Single and joint tax is $1. Later rows are $100 wide. 2025 Tax Rate Table, page T-1.

Stored as 15/1000 so a whole-dollar amount times this rate stays exact to the tenth of a cent before the one half-up round.

Fact.Name: New Mexico residency answers
Fact.Description: Full-year resident is the supported PIT-1. Part-year, first-year, and nonresident returns use Schedule PIT-B and stop. 2025 PIT-1, residency status box 1e: R resident, N non-resident, F first-year, P part-year.

Fact.Name: New Mexico residency
Fact.Description: Full year means you, and your spouse if you file jointly, were New Mexico residents all year. Part-year, first-year, and nonresident stop.

Fact.Name: New Mexico residency is part-year, first-year, or nonresident
Fact.Description: True for Schedule PIT-B. Incomplete until /nmResidencyStatus is answered.

Fact.Name: New Mexico PIT-ADJ addition or deduction
Fact.Description: Yes if the return has a PIT-ADJ addition or deduction. That includes a New Mexico 529 contribution, armed forces active-duty pay, income earned on a reservation or pueblo by a tribal member, and any other New Mexico addition or deduction. PIT-ADJ is not calculated. Yes stops the return. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, lines 11 and 15. Incomplete until answered.

Fact.Name: Credit for income tax paid to another state
Fact.Description: Yes if the filer paid income tax to another state on income New Mexico also taxes. PIT-1 line 20 is not calculated. Yes stops the return. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, line 20. Incomplete until answered.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 9 federal adjusted gross income
Fact.Description: Federal AGI. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, line 9: enter the federal adjusted gross income from Form 1040 or 1040SR.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 zero
Fact.Description: Printed on lines this return does not calculate. Those lines are zero in scope, or the case stops.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 10 state and local tax add-back
Fact.Description: Zero. Itemized deductions stop the return, so the state and local tax add-back is not calculated. 2025 PIT-1, line 10.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 11 additions
Fact.Description: Zero. A PIT-ADJ addition stops the return. 2025 PIT-1, line 11.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 12 federal deduction
Fact.Description: The federal standard deduction, Form 1040 line 12, when the standard deduction applies. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, line 12. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 sets the 2026 amount at $16,100 for a single filer and $32,200 for a joint return. This fact reads the federal standard deduction. Itemized deductions, age 65, blindness, and being claimed as a dependent stop the return.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 13 deduction for certain dependents
Fact.Description: Zero. Dependents stop the return, so the $4,000 deduction is not calculated. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, line 13.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 14 low- and middle-income exemption
Fact.Description: Zero. Federal AGI at or under $36,667 single or $55,000 joint stops the return, so the exemption is not calculated. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, page PIT-1-26.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 15 deductions and exemptions
Fact.Description: Zero. A PIT-ADJ deduction stops the return. 2025 PIT-1, line 15.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 17 New Mexico taxable income
Fact.Description: Add lines 9, 10, and 11, then subtract lines 12, 13, 14, and 15. If the result is negative, enter zero. Lines 10, 11, 13, 14, and 15 are zero, so this is line 9 minus line 12, not below zero. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, line 17.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 17 uses the tax rate table
Fact.Description: True when line 17 is $100,000 or less. The row is the one with lo less than line 17 and line 17 less than or equal to hi. Over $100,000 uses the worksheet.

Fact.Name: Tax rate table row midpoint
Fact.Description: For line 17 over $100, the row is $100 wide and the lookup is lo less than line 17 and line 17 less than or equal to hi. The midpoint is $50 above the $100 boundary below line 17, which is the same as stepping line 17 minus $1 down to a multiple of $100 and adding $50. Line 17 of $43,900 is the top of the $43,800 to $43,900 row, so the midpoint is $43,850. Line 17 of $100 is the top of the $60 to $100 row, so the midpoint is $80. Line 17 of $60 or less uses the midpoint $30. Line 17 of zero uses zero. 2025 Tax Rate Table. Issue 93 comment 7164898822.

Fact.Name: New Mexico tax before the rate portion
Fact.Description: The bracket base for the row midpoint when line 17 is $100,000 or less, or the worksheet base when line 17 is over $100,000. The worksheet bases are the form's figures.

Fact.Name: New Mexico income taxed at the marginal rate
Fact.Description: The row midpoint minus the bracket floor, or line 17 minus the worksheet floor. Not below zero.

Fact.Name: New Mexico marginal rate for this return
Fact.Description: The § 7-2-7 rate for the bracket that contains the row midpoint, or 4.9% or 5.9% on the worksheet.

Fact.Name: New Mexico tax after the cent-then-dollar round
Fact.Description: Round(base plus excess times the rate). Dollar times Rational scales to cents half-even before Round half-up, so a product whose exact fraction is just under half a dollar can become 50 cents and then round up a dollar. This is not always the amount entered on the form.

Fact.Name: One hundred times the exact New Mexico tax
Fact.Description: One hundred times the base, plus the excess times one hundred times the rate. For a whole-dollar excess and these tenth-of-a-percent rates, that product is exact to the tenth of a cent. 4.9% times 100 is 49/10.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 18 New Mexico tax
Fact.Description: One half-up round to the dollar of the table amount or the worksheet amount. The cent-then-dollar result is one dollar high when it exceeds the exact product by more than 50 cents. An exact half dollar stays the half-up dollar. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, line 18. The form says whole dollars only.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 19 lump-sum tax
Fact.Description: Zero. A lump-sum distribution is not W-2 wages and stops with the other-income stop. 2025 PIT-1, line 19.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 20 credit for taxes paid to another state
Fact.Description: Zero. That credit stops the return. 2025 PIT-1, line 20.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 21 business credits
Fact.Description: Zero. Business credits are not in scope. 2025 PIT-1, line 21.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 22 net New Mexico income tax
Fact.Description: Add lines 18 and 19, then subtract lines 20 and 21, not below zero. Those three lines are zero, so this equals line 18. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, line 22.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 23 tax from line 22
Fact.Description: The amount on line 22. 2025 PIT-1, line 23.

Fact.Name: This W-2's New Mexico withholding
Fact.Description: Box 17 when box 15 is New Mexico, the same state as the residence. A blank box 15 is in scope and contributes zero. A box 15 for another state stops the return and contributes zero here.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 27 New Mexico income tax withheld
Fact.Description: Sum of W-2 box 17 where box 15 is New Mexico. 2025 PIT-1, line 27.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 32 total payments and credits
Fact.Description: Add lines 24 through 31. Lines 24, 25, 26, and 28 through 31 are zero, so this equals line 27. The working families tax credit on line 25 is not calculated. The AGI floor keeps a supported return above the credit. 2025 PIT-1, line 32.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 33 tax due
Fact.Description: If line 23 is greater than line 32, the difference. Otherwise zero. 2025 PIT-1, line 33.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 38 tax, penalty, and interest due
Fact.Description: Add lines 33, 34, 36, and 37. Penalty and interest are zero, so this equals line 33. 2025 PIT-1, line 38.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 39 overpayment
Fact.Description: If line 23 is less than line 32, the difference. Otherwise zero. 2025 PIT-1, line 39.

Fact.Name: PIT-1 line 42 refund
Fact.Description: Line 39 minus lines 40 and 41. Contributions are zero, so this equals line 39. 2025 PIT-1, line 42.

Fact.Name: Federal income other than W-2 wages
Fact.Description: Interest, tax-exempt interest, Social Security, a sale or capital gain, 1099-MISC, a 1099-R, Schedule C, or Schedule E. Any of that income stops a PIT-1.

Fact.Name: Dependents or a qualifying person
Fact.Description: Anyone in the household, or a filer who is a qualifying person for the child and dependent care credit. PIT-1 line 13 is $4,000 for certain dependents, and the child income tax credit is on PIT-RC. Neither is calculated.

Fact.Name: Age 65 or blind
Fact.Description: Primary filer is 65 or older or blind. On a joint return, either spouse. The federal additional standard deduction would change line 12, and New Mexico 65-or-older deductions and rebates are on PIT-ADJ and PIT-RC. Those are not calculated. The spouse is checked only on a joint return.

Fact.Name: Filer can be claimed as a dependent
Fact.Description: The primary filer, or either spouse on a joint return. The federal standard deduction for someone who can be claimed as a dependent is limited, so line 12 would not be the ordinary standard deduction. That limited amount is not used. The spouse is checked only on a joint return.

Fact.Name: Filing status other than single or joint
Fact.Description: The supported PIT-1 is single, or married filing jointly with both spouses New Mexico residents all year. Married filing separately and head of household are not calculated. 2025 PIT-1, line 7.

Fact.Name: Federal Schedule 1-A is more than zero
Fact.Description: Qualified tips, overtime, car-loan interest, or the senior deduction on Schedule 1-A line 44. The READY spec calls this stop 1040 line 13b. The 2026 draft Form 1040 in this tool prints Schedule 1-A on line 13a and the qualified business income deduction on line 13b. New Mexico conformity for Schedule 1-A is not pinned, so the deduction is not entered. Incomplete when line 44 is incomplete.

Fact.Name: Federal AGI is at or under the New Mexico exemption ceiling
Fact.Description: $36,667 or less for single. $55,000 or less for married filing jointly. Other filing statuses use the single ceiling and also stop for filing status. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, page PIT-1-26.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: New Mexico part-year, first-year, or nonresident
Fact.Description: Schedule PIT-B is not calculated. Complete false when this is not a New Mexico return. Incomplete until /nmResidencyStatus is answered.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: a W-2 box 15 is not New Mexico
Fact.Description: Any W-2 whose box 15 is a state other than New Mexico. A blank box 15 is in scope and is not this stop. Complete false when this is not a New Mexico return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: income other than W-2 wages
Fact.Description: Any federal income other than W-2 wages. Complete false when this is not a New Mexico return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: dependents
Fact.Description: The line 13 dependent deduction and the child income tax credit are not calculated. Complete false when this is not a New Mexico return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: age 65 or blind
Fact.Description: The additional federal standard deduction and the New Mexico 65-or-older deductions and rebates are not calculated. Complete false when this is not a New Mexico return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: claimed as a dependent
Fact.Description: The limited federal standard deduction for someone who can be claimed as a dependent is not used on line 12. Complete false when this is not a New Mexico return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: filing status other than single or joint
Fact.Description: Married filing separately and head of household are not calculated. Complete false when this is not a New Mexico return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: itemized deductions
Fact.Description: The line 10 state and local tax add-back is not calculated. 2025 PIT-1 instructions, line 12: mark box 12a only if you itemized. Complete false when this is not a New Mexico return. Incomplete until the itemizing choice is answered.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: federal Schedule 1-A
Fact.Description: Schedule 1-A greater than zero stops. The READY spec calls this 1040 line 13b. Complete false when this is not a New Mexico return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: federal AGI at or under the New Mexico exemption ceiling
Fact.Description: Single AGI of $36,667 or less, or joint AGI of $55,000 or less. The line 14 exemption, the low-income comprehensive tax rebate, and the working families tax credit are not calculated. Complete false when this is not a New Mexico return.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: a PIT-ADJ addition or deduction
Fact.Description: PIT-ADJ is not calculated. Complete false when this is not a New Mexico return. Incomplete until the question is answered.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: credit for tax paid to another state
Fact.Description: PIT-1 line 20 is not calculated. Complete false when this is not a New Mexico return. Incomplete until the question is answered.
